wants: Kitchen by the stairs and a bedroom by the window for mom.

grants.name: City of Waterloo ARU Grant, Interior ARU stream
grants.amount: Up to 50% of eligible project costs, maximum $20,000 for an interior unit such as a basement apartment (the Detached ARU stream is up to $30,000).
grants.fitNote: Family members (parent, grandparent, sibling, child, grandchild, aunt/uncle, cousin) can be the tenant if they pay rent at or under the cap and their household income is under the limit; the owner's spouse or a dependent cannot. A rental only fits at the affordable rent for 5 years.
grants.nextStep: Apply before construction starts at https://forms.waterloo.ca/Grants/Apply-for-an-additional-residential-unit-grant ; email ARU@waterloo.ca with questions.

source.title: Apply for the ARU Grant (City of Waterloo)
source.section: Check if you can apply; Review rent and tenant rules; 2026 maximum affordable rent and income

grants.name: Region of Waterloo Ontario Renovates - Secondary Suites (forgivable loan)
grants.amount: Up to $25,000 per property, interest-free, forgiven evenly over 15 years (includes up to $5,000 for accessibility work that is a grant).
grants.fitNote: The Region pitches it for an 'affordable in-law suite', but every occupant is treated as a tenant who must pass income verification and pay rent at or under the cap. Requires the owner to live in the house for 15 years.
grants.nextStep: Confirm zoning with the City, then send the application to OntarioRenovates@regionofwaterloo.ca before any work starts.

source.title: Funding for Secondary Suites (Region of Waterloo)
source.section: Who is eligible; How to apply

grants.name: Multigenerational Home Renovation Tax Credit (MHRTC), line 45355
grants.amount: 14% of up to $50,000 of qualifying costs, so up to $7,000, for a suite finished in 2026 or later (the rate follows the lowest federal tax rate, now 14%; the CRA page still shows 2025's 14.5% and $7,250).
grants.fitNote: Only for a suite that lets a senior (65+) or an adult eligible for the disability tax credit live with a qualifying relative. Not for a rental to an unrelated tenant.
grants.nextStep: Keep all receipts and the permit; claim on line 45355 of the tax return for the year the renovation is completed.

source.title: Line 45355 - Multigenerational home renovation tax credit (CRA)

grants.name: Development charge exemption for a second or third unit in an existing house
grants.amount: City of Waterloo and Region of Waterloo development charges are not charged for a 2nd or 3rd unit in an existing detached, semi-detached or row house (the City charges DCs only on a 4th unit).
grants.nextStep: Nothing to apply for; confirm at permit stage whether any education development charge is billed.

source.title: Development Charges Act, 1997, S.O. 1997, c. 27

grants.name: CMHC-insured refinance for building a secondary suite
grants.amount: Refinance up to 90% of the as-improved home value (value under $2,000,000), amortization up to 30 years; money must go to building the suite.
grants.fitNote: Financing, not free money: it lets you borrow against the finished value. Ask your lender, since only CMHC Approved Lenders offer it.
grants.nextStep: Ask your mortgage lender about the CMHC Refinance for secondary suites before starting construction.

source.title: CMHC Refinance for Building Secondary Suites

process.notes: Conflict between the City web page (homeowner allowed) and the City ARU Guide 2025 p. 20 (architect, engineer or BCIN designer). The Building Code exempts a person designing a house they own from the designer registration requirement (Div. C 3.2.5.1.(3)(b)), which supports the web page.
process.title: Get drawings
process.detail: The City's ARU page lists who may prepare drawings: the homeowner for their own house (up to 2 units), or an architect, engineer or BCIN-qualified designer. The City's 2025 ARU guide says plans must be by an architect, engineer or BCIN designer (conflict; see notes). Drawings: site plan (lot, buildings, dimensioned parking, entrances), floor plans (existing/proposed, wall details, door/window sizes, lintels, ceiling heights, insulation, room names/areas, fixtures, smoke/CO alarm locations, ARU location, fire separation with rating, exits, key plans), structural plans, elevations, cross-section; HVAC (Part 6) design if a unit has 6+ bedrooms.

findings.why: Ceiling height cannot be measured from video.
findings.plain: Ceilings in the new suite must be at least 1.95 m high, and the areas that meet the height must connect to each room's entrance.
findings.title: Ceiling height in the suite: 1.95 m

source.title: 2024 Building Code Compendium (MMAH), Division B

findings.why: Beams and ducts hang below the joists and clearance cannot be measured from video.
findings.plain: Under beams and ductwork inside the suite, the clear height must be at least 1.85 m.
findings.title: Clearance under beams and ducts: 1.85 m

source.title: 2024 Building Code Compendium (MMAH), Division B

findings.why: The bedroom window looks small and high and may not meet the opening size.
findings.plain: Every floor level with a bedroom needs at least one outside window that opens from inside without tools, stays open by itself and gives an unobstructed opening of at least 0.35 m², unless that level has a door straight to the outside.
findings.title: Bedroom escape window: 0.35 m² opening

source.title: 2024 Building Code Compendium (MMAH), Division B

findings.why: The window opening looks small and may be under 380 mm.
findings.plain: The escape window's clear opening must be at least 380 mm in every direction; for sliders, measure only the part that opens.
findings.title: Bedroom escape window: no side under 380 mm

source.title: 2024 Building Code Compendium (MMAH), Division B

findings.why: The inside view cannot show well size or cover.
findings.plain: If the escape window opens into a window well, keep at least 550 mm clear in front of it (beyond any outward-opening sash), and any well cover must open from inside without keys or tools.
findings.title: Window well: 550 mm clear in front

source.title: 2024 Building Code Compendium (MMAH), Division B

fix.description: Install 5/8 in. Type X drywall on the suite ceiling and on both sides of dividing walls, keep it continuous and seal joints and penetrations; add self-closing doors where the separation has openings.

costSource.title: Cost to Make a Basement Legal in Toronto

fix.costNote: Estimate, not a quote (Toronto, 2026, 'fire separation' line). Ceiling drywall installed and finished is $4.00-$6.50/sq ft before the Type X upgrade (see costs[]).

findings.why: Joists and ducts look exposed with no drywalled separation.
findings.plain: Separate the suite from the rest of the house with a 45-minute fire separation, or with a continuous smoke-tight barrier of 15.9 mm (5/8 in.) Type X drywall on both sides of dividing walls and under the floor/ceiling framing. The rating can be waived if the house is sprinklered.
findings.title: Fire/smoke separation between the two homes

source.title: 2024 Building Code Compendium (MMAH), Division B

fix.description: Enclose the furnace/water heater in its own room and line its walls (both sides) and ceiling with 5/8 in. Type X drywall.
fix.costNote: No separate price found; usually part of the fire separation work.

findings.why: Furnace and water heater look open to the basement with no separate room.

check.appliesWhen: a fuel-fired appliance serves both dwelling units

findings.plain: If the furnace or water heater serves both units, put it in a service room lined with 15.9 mm (5/8 in.) Type X drywall on both sides of its walls and on the underside of the ceiling framing; otherwise fuel-fired appliances need a 1-hour fire separation.
findings.title: Furnace room separation

source.title: 2024 Building Code Compendium (MMAH), Division B

fix.description: Install interconnected smoke alarms (hard-wired or wireless) with a visual (strobe) signal in both units and common areas.
fix.costNote: No standalone Ontario price found; one Toronto source bundles alarms into a $4,000-$8,000 electrical line (see costs[]).

findings.why: Smoke alarms in both homes, wired so they all sound together.
findings.plain: Put smoke alarms on every storey, in every bedroom and outside sleeping areas of each unit, and in shared exits and common areas, then interconnect them (hard-wired or wireless) so any one alarm sounds all alarms in both homes.
findings.title: Interconnected smoke alarms in both homes

source.title: 2024 Building Code Compendium (MMAH), Division B

fix.description: Add CO alarms beside each sleeping area in both units and in the furnace room, interconnected across the house.

findings.why: Carbon monoxide alarms near the bedrooms, linked together, when anything burns gas.
findings.plain: If the house has a fuel-burning appliance (such as a gas furnace or water heater) or an attached garage, put CO alarms next to the sleeping rooms in each unit and in the service room, interconnected so one alarm sounds all CO alarms in the house.
findings.title: Interconnected carbon monoxide alarms

source.title: 2024 Building Code Compendium (MMAH), Division B
source.section: 9.32.3.9C.(1) (interconnection within a house with a secondary suite)

findings.why: Stairs and a door are visible but the outside exit path is unclear.
findings.plain: Best: the suite has its own door to the outside. A shared exit is allowed if it is separated by a 30-minute fire separation, does not pass through the other home or a service room, and both homes have interconnected smoke alarms. Leaving through the other home is only allowed with an extra escape window and interconnected alarms, or if the house is sprinklered.
findings.title: A safe way out of the suite

source.title: 2024 Building Code Compendium, Division B Part 11

findings.question: Is there a door from the basement straight outside?
findings.hint: A side door or walk-out that opens to the yard. Not the stairs up to the main floor.

fix.description: Existing house: add a duct-type smoke detector interlocked to shut the furnace's fuel and power. Or give the suite its own heating (separate furnace or ductless heat pump) and seal the duct connections between units.

fix.costNote: Estimate, not a quote, for an independent heating system. Ductless mini-split $3,500-$7,000; firestop and fire dampers $1,000-$3,000. No price found for a duct smoke detector. See costs[].

findings.why: Heating set up so smoke can't travel between the homes: a separate system or a smoke detector in the ducts.
findings.plain: Each home's air ducts may not be directly connected to the other home, and air from one suite may not be recirculated to the other. In a house 5+ years old, one existing forced-air system may serve both if each unit has smoke alarms and a duct smoke detector shuts off the furnace's fuel and power when it detects smoke.
findings.title: No shared air between the homes
